messages:
jess: Heads-up — discovered a parity gap between Go SDK and REST this morning. The sample app's streaming chat path never fires events when using SDK Client.StreamChat(), but curl -> /v1/chat/stream works fine.

alex: oof. which model & SDK version?

jess: go-sdk v0.9.1, model rwd-1-small. Sampleapp uses StreamChat(ctx, req) -> no data until connection closes. No errors in logs.

sam: can you paste the minimal curl you used?

jess: sure:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```
This returns SSE chunks as expected.

mike: sdk side shows we switched to a net.Conn wrapper for streaming last month; maybe a header change broke SSE parsing?

alex: iirc the SDK sets `Accept: application/json` for stream calls accidentally. That would suppress SSE on server side. jess can you dump the raw request headers from the SDK?

jess: grabbed a tcpdump + logs. SDK request headers: `Authorization: Bearer ...`, `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Connection: keep-alive`. REST curl uses `Accept: text/event-stream`.

sam: that's the bug. server decides streaming mode based on Accept. we changed default Accept in go-sdk to be explicit json for non-stream paths but didn't special-case stream endpoints.

mike: beyond the header bug, we should check retry/backoff differences — i saw retries for 502 behave differently between SDK and REST where SDK retries immediately but REST uses a 1s jitter. that could impact long-poll streaming resiliency.

jess: also noticed param drift: sampleapp sets `max_tokens` as an int pointer; via REST we send `max_tokens: 512`, but SDK serializes absent optional ints as `null` sometimes. leads to server-side defaulting differences.

alex: ugh. sequence: header Accept mismatch -> no SSE -> client falls back to long poll (or just waits) -> eventually closes -> retry logic kicks in with different timing. multiple gaps.

sam: proposed fixes:
- go-sdk: special-case stream APIs to set `Accept: text/event-stream` and validate raw body reader returns chunks (unit test).
- go-sdk: normalize optional numeric params so that omitted != null; follow REST wire behavior.
- add an e2e sampleapp test matrix (curl vs sdk) for streaming/chat/embeds.

mike: +1. add a quick compatibility test in CI: spin up envoy mock that expects SSE and fails if Accept != text/event-stream.

jess: small repro attached in gist (link) and a failing sampleapp branch. I've flagged the sampleapp test as flaky in CI until we patch.

alex: who wants the SDK PR? i can do header fix + test today. sam can you handle numeric param serialization? mike can you add the CI check?

sam: i'll take serialization. quick note: make sure to run `go vet` + unit tests — we have one subtle marshal hook in encoder.go that treats zero value ints as omitted. we need to only omit when pointer==nil not when value==0.

mike: i'll add the CI assert and a small regression job to run sampleapp against curl. devex-bot: please create issues for these? :devex-bot: 

devex-bot: Created issues: DEX-312 (go-sdk streaming Accept header), DEX-313 (go-sdk numeric param serialization), DEX-314 (CI streaming acceptance test).

jess: thanks. i'll keep sampleapp branch open and link the PRs. after fixes, can we add a short DX doc for onboarding — note streaming gotcha + how to verify headers? new hires hit this and it's a frustrating first-hour debugging flow.

alex: agreed. add a short checklist to the quickstart: "verify stream responses with curl before assuming SDK is wrong" and include the `Accept:` bit.

sam: FYI I'll add a tiny unit test that compares SDK-serialized payload vs our REST fixture for 4 shapes (chat stream, chat non-stream, embeddings, create session). Should cut down parity regressions.

mike: timeline? alex?

alex: header PR in today, sam's serialization fix by EOD. CI job by mike tomorrow morning. i'll review all.

jess: perfect. thanks team :thumbsup:

mike: follow-up: ticket DEX-315 to add a telemetry metric when server falls back from SSE to json body so we can detect in prod if clients are hitting this mismatch.

alex: good call. logging + metric will help catch other SDKs too.

jess: closing loop here. if anyone hits more odd streaming behavior, drop it in this thread and paste raw headers.
